edbDesc: The phenomenon that small particles suspended in gas (aerosols) or liquids (hydrocolloids) starts to migrate when illuminated by a sufficiently intense beam of light. The existence of this phenomenon is owed to a non-uniform distribution of temperature of an illuminated particle in a fluid medium.
title: Photophoresis
description: Tiny specks of dust or smoke drift along a strong light beam, or even against it, because the side the light heats pushes harder on the surrounding gas. Felix Ehrenhaft described it in 1918. Researchers use it to trap and steer single particles in mid-air, including a 2018 display that draws glowing 3D images with a laser-held speck.
effect: light heating one side of a tiny particle in a gas pushes the particle along
usedIn: Sorting aerosol particles by how they absorb light
Proposed light-lofted micro-flyers in the upper atmosphere
strength: Only works on specks smaller than about a hair's width, but there it can beat gravity and hold soot particles aloft.
pickWhy: Borderline: Judgment call: same gas push as the deck's Crookes radiometer, so in-deck is arguable; picked keep because it moves free particles, a different job with new uses.
